title: Business compatibility in the destiny matrix: a deal read from two dates

seo.title: Destiny matrix business compatibility by date of birth
seo.description: Destiny matrix business compatibility: the partners’ dates are added directly. What each point means, from the partnership’s base to the money outcome.
queries: business compatibility by date of birth

short: Business compatibility in the destiny matrix is counted differently from love compatibility. The two people’s matrices are not added together: the dates of birth themselves are — day to day, month to month, year to year — and an ordinary matrix is built on the resulting “date”. It describes not the two people but the venture between them: what the partnership stands on, what the deal can bring, what you will have to accept and what the financial outcome will be. The calculation and the meanings of the points follow the chapter on atypical compatibility in Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book.

sections.h2: How business compatibility differs from love compatibility
paragraphs: In love compatibility every point of the couple’s matrix is the sum of the same points of two personal charts. That matrix describes a union: the atmosphere between the partners, their shared tasks, home life, family money.

For business Lisovskaya takes another route. A deal, a joint project or a partnership is a third party with its own “date of birth”, and that date is found by adding the two dates together. So the same two people almost always have different love and business matrices: they may live together easily and work together with difficulty — or the other way round.
The business matrix does not say whether the people are good in themselves. It shows what character their shared venture takes on and where its supports, gains and friction lie.

sections.h2: How the business matrix is calculated
paragraphs: The dates are added part by part. The example from the book: 20.05.1987 and 29.12.1973.

ul: **Day:** 20 + 29 = 49; above 22, so the digits are added: 4 + 9 = 13.
**Month:** 5 + 12 = 17. The month is not reduced to 12 here: in the business “date” it is simply a number, and 17 stays 17.
**Year:** 1987 + 1973 = 3960, and the digits of the year are added: 3 + 9 + 6 + 0 = 18.

paragraphs: The result is the “date” 13.17.18, and an ordinary matrix is built on it: day, month and year become points of the outer square, the bottom point is their sum (13 + 17 + 18 = 48 → 12), and the centre is the sum of all four (60 → 6). In the book this example has a bottom point of 8 and a centre of 11 — a misprint: by the chapter’s own rule 13 + 17 + 18 = 48 → 12. The block of purposes is not calculated for a business matrix.
Lisovskaya also adds a person’s date of birth to the date of a contract or of a company’s founding. The site’s calculator works with two dates of birth.
The points are read from the author’s table in the section on deals and business partners. The names are the same as in the “Compatibility at work” section on the site.

ul: **What the partnership stands on** — the centre of the matrix. The main support of the shared venture: what it falls apart without.
**How your partner sees you** — the day point. How the other side perceives you and where your advantage lies in their eyes.
**The upside of the deal** — the month point. What you achieve together if the venture goes well; read only in the plus.
**What you will have to accept** — the bottom point. The downsides that come with the deal; read only in the minus.
**Material gain** — the year point. What the partnership gives both of you in money and goods.
**Result and benefit** — where the shared venture leads and what remains at the end.
**Difficulties of working together** — where friction arises and what conflicts may rest on.
**What may stay behind the scenes** — two points read together: what the other side may not tell you and what to prepare for.
**Financial outcome** — the money line of three points, read as a whole: the way into money, the path to profit and the outcome of the deal.
**How to reach agreement** — the relationship line: what unites you and on what terms to work so that respect holds.

sections.h2: How to read a business matrix
paragraphs: Start with the base. The centre answers the main question — what the partnership will stand on — and the other points are read through it: if the support is order and agreements, difficulties will most often grow out of breaking them.

Then look at the pair “upside — downside”. The upside shows why you enter the deal, the bottom point shows the price you will pay for it. A decision is made looking at both at once: a hard energy in the downside is not a ban but a condition worth knowing in advance.

Difficulties of working together and the hidden points are a practical checklist: where to write the contract in more detail, what to check before signing, what to agree on out loud. Read the money line as a whole, from the way in to the outcome: its points taken one by one give an incomplete picture.

For a one-off deal the upside, the downside and the financial outcome matter most. For a long partnership it is the base, the relationship line and the difficulties: they decide how you will get through years of working together.

sections.h2: Example: the two dates from the calculator
paragraphs: The dates 31.03.1993 and 28.12.1994 are the calculator’s example. Day: 31 + 28 = 59 → 14. Month: 3 + 12 = 15. Year: 1993 + 1994 = 3987 → 27 → 9. The business “date” is 14.15.9.

ul: **Base — 13.** The partnership stands on a readiness to change: closing directions that have run their course, rebuilding processes, not clinging to what once worked.
**How your partner sees you — 14.** As a person of measure who smooths out extremes and finds the middle that works.
**Upside of the deal — 15.** Scale, strong money and influence: the venture can grow bigger than you planned.
**What you will have to accept — 11.** Working at the limit of your strength: pressure, stubbornness, having to pull the load yourselves when others tire.

**Financial outcome — 22, 5, 10.** The way into money is through the new and unconventional, the path to profit runs through rules, contracts and the experience of elders, and the outcome comes in waves: good periods give way to downturns.

paragraphs: So one matrix adds up to a working picture: great potential and money, provided the partners are ready to change course and carry the load, and plan for the financial waves in advance.

sections.h2: Where to calculate compatibility at work
paragraphs: The “Compatibility at work” section is part of the [compatibility calculator](/compatibility): enter two dates of birth, and below the love part of the reading a business matrix appears with spheres of its own. Two are open without a purchase — what the partnership stands on and the upside of the deal; the other eight open with the full couple reading.

The numbers in the points are ordinary arcana. What each number means on its own is on the arcana pages; what it means in a couple is in the section [“Arcana in compatibility”](/encyclopedia/compatibility).

faq.q: Can I calculate compatibility with a colleague or a boss?
faq.a: Yes, the calculation is the same: two dates of birth are added, and the business matrix shows how your work together will go. For a team Lisovskaya adds the dates of all members — the site has no such calculation; the calculator works for two people.

faq.q: Why can the month in a business date be greater than 12?
faq.a: Because it is not a calendar month but the sum of two months. In a business matrix the twelve-month rule does not apply: 5 + 12 = 17, and the point holds 17 — The Star.

faq.q: Can I calculate by the date a company was registered or a contract was signed?
faq.a: In the book, yes: Lisovskaya adds a person’s date to the date of a contract or a founding. The site’s calculator is built for two dates of birth; if you enter a registration date in the second field, read only the “Compatibility at work” section — the love part does not apply to such a calculation.

faq.q: If the downside holds a hard arcanum, is it better not to make the deal?
faq.a: No. The book reads the bottom point only in the minus, so every pair has the price of the deal there. It shows what to prepare for; it does not forbid working together.

faq.q: How does compatibility at work differ from ordinary couple compatibility?
faq.a: Love compatibility adds two matrices point by point and describes a union. Business compatibility adds the dates and describes the shared venture as a separate object: the partnership’s support, the gain, the downsides of the deal and the financial outcome.
